decision: Retain original adaptive MTP on the forward compatibility-fix image. Three samples per arm/cell show standalone GPU copy loses 32.3% prose and 50.1% code decode, and 51.6%/58.3% C4 aggregate throughput at 2K/8K. Only exact repetition at 8K improves (+8.0%); edited code and prose regress with separated observed ranges. Copy cold prefill improves 2.6%/2.3%, insufficient to offset generation loss. All three visits pass short/8K/32K/128K numerical gates and functional/cancellation checks. Target verifier, weights, target precision, context and qualified E3/transport settings are retained; no older image is restored.

limitations: Three measurements per cell and arm, with MTP bracketing one copy boot; not a many-boot confidence interval.

The first MTP control predates a ngram-only configuration-validation repair. Remaining arms use the repaired image; target kernels/weights/precision and the MTP validation path are unchanged. Both images receive full numerical gates.
The synthetic repetitive/edit workloads favor prompt lookup; prose is the non-copy control. All retain low reasoning.
Fixed output budgets measure throughput, not completed-task quality; separate functional and numerical receipts apply.
SSE decode timing is an estimate; a speculative step can emit multiple tokens.
Server decode and wall timings include drafting, target verification and scheduling; no isolated GPU proposal timer.

For GPU ngram, worker-local trimming does not update the engine-core scheduled-slot list. The public draft-token counter can include invalid/no-match slots; unaccepted slots are not an exact count of valid copies rejected by the target. Accepted tokens and end-to-end rates remain separately reported.
Memory minima are observed guard samples, not guaranteed global minima.

configuration_repair.original_failure: SpeculativeConfig revalidates an alias of target model as a draft even for ngram, before full TP6 target head padding. No copy speed or quality result exists.

counter_limitation: Keep raw metrics. Public reporting labels the counter as reported draft slots and the difference from accepted tokens as slots not accepted. Do not claim every such slot was a real proposed copy rejected by the target. Exact valid-proposal rejection and isolated proposer GPU time are not measured. Wall rates and accepted tokens per wall/server decode time include all observed overhead.
hybrid_assessment: Do not build a hybrid in this goal. The 8K exact-repeat gain is narrow (+8.0%, about 55.9 versus 51.8 output tok/s); 2K repetition, edited code, prose and both C4 mixes regress. Per-request routing and shared proposal scheduling would add unmeasured costs and compatibility work. A future hybrid needs a new selector/cost hypothesis and repeated mixed-workload evidence.
